description: Waves 15–16 combined executable queue. Wave 15 (US-326..373) ships the complete casual consumer game: truthful multi-human seating, immutable custom role/rules snapshots, OpenRouter catalog/selection and exact routing audit, encrypted BYOK, one-time $5 verified-account promotional credit with integer-micro ledger and bounded completion reserve, and a neo-noir occult-laboratory + sleek technical UI targeting 20–30 minute games. Wave 16 (US-374..407) starts only after the Wave 15 full-product gate and ships server-owned ranked modes: exact-route AI scientific OpenRouter campaigns, frozen ranked seasons/pools/AI anchors, standardized solo human-vs-AI, strangers-only mixed human/AI DB-backed matchmaking, calibrated season/mode ratings, safety/report/block, deterministic season-stream rollback, shadow/load/canary gates. Locked decisions live in prd-v4.md. All production ranked flags remain OFF until explicit operator go/no-go.

userStories.title: Pure lobby seat-claim plan and invariants
userStories.description: Define the pure deterministic transition that assigns a joining LobbyMember to one available AI lobby seat and the inverse transition that releases the member back to an AI slot. This closes the discovered membership-without-seat defect before any UI/OpenRouter work stacks on lobbies.
acceptanceCriteria: A pure core function assigns the lowest-index eligible AI seat to a joining member and returns an immutable seat plan; identical input yields identical output.
It rejects full lobbies, duplicate member seating, malformed layouts, and attempts to replace a host/reserved human seat with stable reason tokens.
The inverse transition releases exactly the departing member's seat, clears member ownership, and preserves any host-configured AI model reservation policy defined by the input.
Property tests cover one-member-one-seat, unique seat indices, human count equals seated member count, and join/release round trips; no DB/network/clock/random imports enter core.
userStories.notes: Test-first. Likely files: core/lobby/seating.py, tests/core/lobby/test_seating.py.

userStories.title: Atomically seat invited members on join
userStories.description: Apply the pure seat plan inside the existing lobby join transaction so every first-time invited member immediately owns a real HUMAN LobbySeat. Capacity is checked under row locks and concurrent last-seat joins cannot overbook.
acceptanceCriteria: A first successful join converts one available LobbySeat to HUMAN and sets member_id in the same transaction that inserts LobbyMember.
An idempotent rejoin returns the existing member/seat without claiming another admission or seat.
Two concurrent joins for the last slot yield one success and one stable lobby_full response on Postgres; SQLite coverage proves serialized correctness without relying on SKIP LOCKED.
A failed/rolled-back join leaves neither an unseated member nor a claimed seat/admission reservation.
Existing counts-only composition reports the new human count but discloses no in-game public seat mapping.
userStories.notes: BLOCKER. Likely files: api/routes/lobbies.py, db/repositories/lobbies.py, tests/api/test_lobby_invite_presence.py, postgres concurrency test.

userStories.title: Release and reassign seats across lobby lifecycle
userStories.description: Make kick, stale eviction, leave, host transfer, and abandoned-lobby cleanup maintain member/seat integrity. A vacated human slot becomes an AI slot eligible for deterministic refill or a later human join.
acceptanceCriteria: Kick and explicit leave release the target member's LobbySeat and admission reservations atomically.
Stale-member reconciliation releases seats before deleting members; no LobbySeat retains a dangling member_id.
Host transfer moves host authority only and never moves or duplicates seat ownership.
A later invited member can claim the released slot; configured AI model selection is preserved or cleared according to the pure release input and covered by tests.
Lifecycle operations are idempotent under retries and concurrent kick/heartbeat/leave races.
userStories.notes: Add a member leave endpoint if absent. Likely files: lobbies routes/repo, lobby_presence, tests.

userStories.title: Fail-closed launch-readiness invariant for every lobby member
userStories.description: Replace aggregate ready-up assumptions with one canonical launch-readiness check: every active LobbyMember owns exactly one HUMAN seat, every HUMAN seat resolves to an active member, every AI seat has or can resolve a model, capacity matches the rules snapshot, and every seated human is present/ready.
acceptanceCriteria: A pure readiness evaluator returns allowed plus a stable ordered reason list for missing seat, duplicate seat, orphan seat, absent/not-ready member, unresolved AI seat, or count mismatch.
Lock and launch both invoke the evaluator and fail closed; direct repository corruption cannot materialize a malformed Game.
The host cannot launch merely because aggregate ready counts match when a member is unseated.
Ranked/custom mode policy is injected as facts; the pure evaluator imports no DB/settings/clock.
Tests cover 1–N humans for every built-in player count and malformed layouts.
userStories.notes: Likely files: core/lobby/readiness.py, api/lobby_launch.py, routes/lobbies.py.

userStories.title: Player-facing lobby member identity without in-game seat leakage
userStories.description: Replace shortened internal member UUIDs in member-scoped lobby views with safe player-facing display labels while retaining the anonymity firewall between lobby membership and in-game public seat ids.
acceptanceCriteria: Lobby roster returns member_id plus caller-safe display_label, is_self, host, ready, and present; it never returns Principal id/email, GameSeat public_player_id, AI seat mapping, provider, or model-to-seat mapping.
Duplicate/blank display names receive deterministic lobby-local disambiguators without mutating global identity.
Only members can read the roster; non-members still receive existence-hiding 404.
Anonymous launch reshuffles/publicly maps seats independently so lobby ordering cannot reveal which public seat is human.
API and frontend tests assert full-JSON absence of forbidden identity columns.
userStories.notes: Member list may identify invited humans before play; rule 7 still forbids binding them to game seats.

userStories.title: Production multi-human adapter, presence, and takeover coverage
userStories.description: Prove and harden the human worker for multiple simultaneous HUMAN seats rather than the single-host path. Each human adapter polls only its principal-authorized seat and disconnect takeover remains per seat.
acceptanceCriteria: build_human_lane_adapter constructs one distinct HumanAdapter per HUMAN seat and one AI adapter assignment per AI seat for a 2+ human game.
Action/chat authorization rejects cross-principal game-seat submissions even when both principals belong to the same lobby.
Presence heartbeats and grace expiry take over only the disconnected seat; connected humans remain human-controlled.
A process restart rehydrates multiple buffered human actions/chat holds and preserves deadlines/hash head.
Tests exercise simultaneous submissions and one-seat takeover without timing flakiness.
userStories.notes: Likely files: runner/human_lane.py, human_seat_auth.py, presence repositories/tests.

userStories.title: Real two- and three-human end-to-end games
userStories.description: Add default-suite end-to-end coverage that enters humans through real HTTP invite flows, seats them, readies, launches, drives independent actions/chat, reaches terminal, reveals, and replays.
acceptanceCriteria: A deterministic 2-human mini7 game completes through actual guest/account cookies and DB-backed HumanAdapters.
A deterministic 3-human game covers one disconnect/takeover while the other humans finish.
Every joined human receives exactly one GameSeat occupant_principal_id and can retrieve only their observation.
Pre-reveal frames remain identity-blind; reveal identifies humans/models as allowed; chat stays sidecar-only.
Both games write zero Rating/RatingEvent and zero HumanRating/HumanRatingEvent rows because custom games are casual; replay verifies byte-identically.
userStories.notes: Wave 15 multiplayer truth gate; tests use mock AI and injected clocks, never real providers.

userStories.title: Immutable GameRulesSnapshot core contract
userStories.description: Introduce one frozen pure rules value used by built-ins and custom decks. It contains the exact mechanical/cadence inputs required for setup, phase progression, legal actions, observations, and replay, plus canonical serialization/hash.
acceptanceCriteria: GameRulesSnapshot is frozen, contains no floats in its canonical event representation, and validates role multiset, faction mapping, win-condition identifiers, limits, discussion cycles, and cadence id.
Every built-in get_ruleset result projects to a snapshot whose behavior matches the module constants in existing golden tests.
canonical_rules_hash is sha256 of sorted compact UTF-8 JSON and custom ruleset_id is custom:<hash>.
Unknown roles/actions/win-condition identifiers fail closed before game creation.
Pure-core firewall and canonical byte-stability tests cover the new type.
userStories.notes: Do not make core query a DB registry. Likely files: core/rulesets/snapshot.py.

userStories.title: Persist lobby/game rules snapshots (migration 0065)
userStories.description: Migration 0065 adds immutable rules snapshot JSON/hash fields to lobbies and games, with safe nullable/backfill behavior for existing rows. Built-in games reconstruct the identical snapshot when legacy fields are absent.
acceptanceCriteria: 0065 is the sole new linear migration after 0064; upgrade/downgrade work on SQLite and Postgres.
New lobbies persist rules_snapshot_json and rules_snapshot_hash together; new games copy them at launch.
DB constraints/repository validation reject hash/body disagreement and mutation after launch.
Legacy games with null snapshots continue resolving their registered ruleset_id byte-identically.
No snapshot contains timestamps, credentials, funding balances, provider routing, or player identity.
userStories.notes: Likely files: db models/migration/repositories and migration-head tests.

userStories.title: Pure custom supported-role deck validator
userStories.description: Allow custom casual hosts to compose a deck from implemented Role enum members while preventing mechanically undefined or degenerate games. Validation derives factions/win-condition template only from supported declarative definitions.
acceptanceCriteria: Validator accepts supported role counts for 7–15 seats and produces a GameRulesSnapshot with deterministic sorted role representation.

It rejects roles lacking complete legal-action/NAR/observation support, zero-town/zero-threat decks, impossible win conditions, invalid faction ratios, unsupported solo-role combinations, and player-count mismatch with stable reason tokens.
It explicitly permits duplicate ordinary roles where mechanics support them and pins uniqueness constraints for roles that require them.
Mayor/Framer/Commuter/Mason or other gated roles remain unavailable until their existing variance/mechanics gate says enabled; UI capability derives from the same result.
Table/property tests cover every currently implemented role and pairwise interaction-sensitive deck.
userStories.notes: Arbitrary executable/user-authored roles remain out of scope.

userStories.title: Run and replay games from persisted rules snapshots
userStories.description: Thread GameRulesSnapshot through game configuration, setup, reducer/resolvers, observations, human rehydration, and replay so custom games never need a live DB/catalog lookup to rediscover mechanics.
acceptanceCriteria: A custom:<hash> game runs to terminal using only its persisted snapshot plus events.
Engine replay and frozen-response replay accept the archived snapshot and reproduce state/hash head without get_ruleset(custom_id).
Registered built-in games remain byte-identical and existing golden hashes do not change.
Mismatch between requested ruleset_id and snapshot hash fails before an event is appended.
No DB/network import is added under core; impure shells load and inject the snapshot.
userStories.notes: Large seam story but bounded to rules injection; no UI/API deck builder here.

userStories.title: Custom lobby configuration API with role deck and seat mix
userStories.description: Replace the minimal LobbyCreate contract with an explicit casual custom configuration: role deck or built-in preset, cadence preset, identity mode, theme, desired human slots, and AI slots. Ranked is forbidden on this route.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /lobbies accepts either built_in_ruleset_id or custom_role_counts, never both, and returns normalized rules summary plus validation errors.
Host selects a human seat capacity from 1..player_count; remaining slots are AI. Joins cannot exceed human capacity.
The custom route always binds a non-ranked HUMANS_INCLUDED league and rejects ranked=true/unknown fields; the old ranked checkbox contract is deprecated without reopening a hidden path.
Configuration freezes after first non-host join except safe theme/cosmetic changes; lock freezes everything.
API response remains member-scoped and does not expose eventual in-game seat mapping.
userStories.notes: Coordinate backward compatibility for existing clients/tests.

userStories.title: Phase-specific 20–30 minute casual cadence
userStories.description: Replace the one global human phase deadline with a frozen cadence profile for standard casual play. Several short deterministic discussion cycles per day target a 20–30 minute match without adding wall-clock reads to core.
acceptanceCriteria: A pure cadence profile maps phase kind/round to deadline seconds, release delay, and UI countdown label; standard casual defaults are documented in code and sum to the target range at MAX_DAYS.
Human runner snapshots the per-phase deadline from injected now and resumes it across restart without extending an existing deadline.
Humans may submit multiple sidecar chat messages within a discussion cycle subject to existing limits; each AI produces at most the rules-defined message/action response for that cycle.
Timeout coercion remains deterministic and never parses chat into actions.
Fast/standard/relaxed casual presets are supported; ranked cadence is not player-configurable and lands in Wave 16.
userStories.notes: Use existing round-based engine, not an unbounded continuous-chat scheduler.

userStories.title: Custom rules, cadence, and segregation end-to-end proof
userStories.description: Exercise a non-built-in supported role deck through lobby create, multi-human seating, launch, advanced legal action, terminal result, archived snapshot, and replay.
acceptanceCriteria: Test creates a custom deck containing at least one non-mini7 active role and proves its legal action/NAR effect occurs.
The game uses the selected cadence profile and survives rehydration mid-phase.
Archived rules snapshot/hash is sufficient for replay after monkeypatching live ruleset resolution to fail.
Custom game updates personal casual stats only and writes zero human/scientific ratings.
Malformed custom deck is rejected before Lobby/Game/Event rows are written.
userStories.notes: Default-suite deterministic integration test.

userStories.title: Honor database provider endpoints and secret references generically
userStories.description: Remove the hardcoded four-provider runtime choke point. Project ModelProvider base_url/auth_secret_ref through the AgentBuild runtime value and construct adapters from persisted provider configuration.
acceptanceCriteria: project_agent_build carries provider name, base_url, and an opaque auth_secret_ref into the impure adapter assembly without resolving or serializing raw secret material.
build_heterogeneous_adapter accepts any configured provider rather than indexing a hardcoded provider map; existing Cerebras/DeepInfra/Xiaomi/Z.AI behavior remains compatible.
Unknown/missing/insecure secret references fail at adapter construction before a game starts with redacted errors.
Provider rows/read APIs never return auth_secret_ref to players/spectators.
Tests register a synthetic OpenAI-compatible provider and complete a stubbed heterogeneous call.
userStories.notes: Security prerequisite for OpenRouter.

userStories.title: OpenRouter settings and adapter request policy
userStories.description: Add first-class OpenRouter endpoint/config support through the existing LiteLLM/OpenAI-compatible seam, including app attribution, router metadata opt-in, ZDR, provider preferences, and required-parameter enforcement.
acceptanceCriteria: Settings define optional inference key ref, optional management key ref, base URL, app URL/title, default ZDR=true for human games, timeout, and catalog sync interval; no real key default/fixture.
OpenRouter requests use the canonical model slug, explicit api_base/api_key, HTTP-Referer/X-OpenRouter-Title, and X-OpenRouter-Metadata enabled.
Routing policy can express sort/order/only/allow_fallbacks/require_parameters/max_price/zdr as validated data and passes it without leaking into core events.
Casual defaults permit router fallback within the selected model; scientific/ranked policies can disable it later.
Stubbed tests assert exact request kwargs/headers and redacted failure logs.
userStories.notes: Use existing dependencies; no OpenRouter SDK required.

userStories.title: Persist immutable OpenRouter catalog snapshots (migration 0066)
userStories.description: Migration 0066 adds catalog snapshot and model-entry tables that preserve the exact OpenRouter discovery data used when a lobby/game is configured.
acceptanceCriteria: 0066 follows 0065 linearly and has SQLite/Postgres upgrade/downgrade coverage.

CatalogSnapshot stores fetched_at outside core, canonical content hash, source ETag/version when available, and status; ModelCatalogEntry stores canonical slug, display name, description, modalities, context, pricing strings/micros, supported params, provider summary, expiration, and raw normalized metadata.
A snapshot is immutable after completion and duplicate content hashes are idempotent.
No API key, request authorization header, account credit, or player identifier is persisted in catalog tables.
Indexes support canonical_slug lookup and filtered/paginated catalog browsing.
0066 also reserves the append-only ModelProbeEvidence table keyed by model/catalog/prompt/schema/probe-suite so later probe stories never edit this shipped migration.
userStories.notes: Pricing conversion must be decimal/string based, never float balance math.

userStories.title: Catalog sync service, CLI, and stale-last-good behavior
userStories.description: Implement an async OpenRouter Models API synchronizer with conditional fetch, validation, atomic snapshot publication, and a CLI/admin trigger. Runtime browsing always reads the last complete snapshot.
acceptanceCriteria: Successful sync validates the full response then atomically marks one immutable snapshot complete; readers never see a partial catalog.
Unchanged content is idempotent; network/schema/rate-limit failure preserves and serves last-good with freshness metadata.
CLI command returns counts/hash/fetched time without printing credentials or raw headers; default tests use MockTransport.
Text-output models are retained even without structured output; non-text-only models are excluded from play catalog.
Concurrent sync attempts serialize or dedupe under Postgres and SQLite.
userStories.notes: Do not make game launch depend on live OpenRouter availability.

userStories.title: Player model-catalog API with search, filters, and price metadata
userStories.description: Expose a human-session-safe catalog API designed for the selector, not the admin AgentBuild API.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /human/models supports stable keyset pagination, free-text name/slug search, provider, price, context, structured-output, tier, privacy, and availability filters.

Entries expose canonical slug, display fields, pricing per million, context, supported capabilities, qualification tier/reasons, expiration, and catalog freshness; no internal UUID or secret reference is required to select.
Unknown/stale/deprecated states are explicit and fail closed for platform eligibility.
Anonymous scraping is rate limited; authenticated users get the same model facts without account/key metadata.
Tests cover combined filters, pagination stability, escaping, stale catalog, and no-secret full JSON.
userStories.notes: Catalog can be public later; human-scoped first limits abuse.

userStories.title: Pure compatibility and qualification tier policy
userStories.description: Create one deterministic policy deriving UNVERIFIED, PLAYABLE, VERIFIED_STRUCTURED, or RANKED_QUALIFIED from catalog facts plus probe evidence and operator policy.
acceptanceCriteria: All text models enter UNVERIFIED casual visibility unless explicitly disabled/deprecated; no model is claimed compatible solely from popularity.
PLAYABLE requires a successful schema/coercion probe within token/latency bounds; VERIFIED_STRUCTURED additionally requires advertised+observed strict schema support.

RANKED_QUALIFIED requires verified structured output, pinned provider availability, price/latency limits, minimum successful sample, and no unresolved drift; Wave 15 computes but does not use it for ratings.
Policy returns ordered reason tokens and is deterministic with injected facts/time bucket.
Boundary tests cover missing/lying supported_parameters, free models, extreme pricing, expiration, and probe drift.
userStories.notes: Pure core policy; network/database shells only resolve facts.

userStories.title: Compatibility probe runner and evidence history
userStories.description: Add an operator-triggered/background probe that sends canonical role/action observations to a model through stub-friendly OpenRouter transport and records append-only evidence without affecting games.
acceptanceCriteria: Probe suite covers JSON contract, one public message, vote, each supported night-action family, token usage, latency, and refusal/error behavior.
Evidence stores catalog snapshot, prompt/schema hashes, provider/routing facts, result hashes/status, tokens/cost, and observed_at; raw credential absent.
A probe failure demotes derived eligibility but never edits old evidence or active in-flight game snapshots.
Default suite uses deterministic fake responses; real probes are opt-in integration tests with explicit spend cap.
Admin/CLI trigger is rate/cost limited and idempotent for the same model+suite+catalog+prompt tuple.
userStories.notes: Uses the ModelProbeEvidence table deliberately created by US-342 migration 0066; never edit 0066 after it ships.

userStories.title: Idempotent on-demand AgentBuild materialization (migration 0067)
userStories.description: Resolve a selected canonical slug plus rules snapshot/prompt version into a reusable AgentBuild/ModelConfig under the OpenRouter provider, eliminating UUID entry from player workflows. Migration 0067 adds the database uniqueness/hash fields needed to make concurrent materialization authoritative.
acceptanceCriteria: Service get_or_create is unique/idempotent for provider, canonical slug, catalog snapshot policy, prompt version, adapter version, and inference params hash.
It refuses non-text/deprecated/disabled models and stamps qualification tier/catalog snapshot used at creation.
Display/version fields are derived from canonical catalog data, not player input; inference params are allowlisted and bounded.
Concurrent calls return one logical build on Postgres/SQLite without duplicate rows.
Existing admin-created builds and scientific identities remain readable and are not silently rewritten.
0067 follows 0066 linearly, adds/backfills nullable identity-hash fields safely, and has SQLite/Postgres upgrade/downgrade plus uniqueness-race coverage.
userStories.notes: Owns migration 0067; do not weaken concurrency to application-only read-then-insert.

userStories.title: Select lobby AI seats by canonical model slug
userStories.description: Replace prepick_agent_build_ids in the player contract with per-slot canonical model selections and optional safe routing preferences. Launch resolves/materializes builds and freezes runtime selections.
acceptanceCriteria: Lobby create/update accepts model_slug per AI slot or an autofill policy; no player-facing AgentBuild UUID input remains.
Duplicate model slugs are allowed in casual custom lobbies and produce distinct seats backed by the same immutable build where appropriate.
Selections resolve against one catalog snapshot and freeze requested slug, catalog id, prompt/schema hashes, inference params, routing policy, and funding owner reference without secret material.
Changing the live catalog or model availability after lock does not mutate the frozen lobby; launch gives a clear unavailable-before-lock failure.
Auto-fill chooses deterministically from platform/BYOK eligible models under injected price/compatibility policy.
userStories.notes: Model identity may be visible in pregame configuration but never bound to public in-game seat before reveal.

userStories.title: Persist actual OpenRouter routing metadata (migration 0068)
userStories.description: Migration 0068 extends LlmCall/runtime audit data to distinguish requested model from actual provider/model and archive router attempt metadata required for cost/scientific attribution.
acceptanceCriteria: 0068 follows 0067 linearly; upgrade/downgrade and ORM export tests pass.

Each OpenRouter call records requested canonical slug, actual model/provider/endpoint when supplied, generation id, router strategy/attempt/is_byok, normalized attempts/pipeline, catalog snapshot id, and routing-policy hash.
Metadata is bounded/sanitized JSON and excludes auth headers, credentials, prompt content duplicated outside existing retention policy, and provider secrets.
Non-OpenRouter calls remain compatible with nullable fields.
Retention/export/privacy tests specify which metadata persists and prove no human credential/key hash is exposed.
userStories.notes: OpenRouter router metadata is impure audit data, excluded from core event hashes.

userStories.title: Deterministic whole-game cost estimator
userStories.description: Build a pure conservative estimator that uses rules/cadence snapshot, AI seat selections, catalog token prices, context growth bounds, max output tokens, fixed/request/reasoning charges, and safety margin to produce a per-seat and whole-game maximum reservation.
acceptanceCriteria: Estimator uses integer USD micros and decimal parsing only; no float arithmetic, DB, clock, or network.
Result includes low/expected/reservation totals, per-seat breakdown, assumptions, catalog hash, and stable reason tokens for unpriceable/over-policy models.
Worst-case call counts derive from the frozen rules/cadence snapshot and alive-seat upper bounds; tests pin mini7/bench10/custom deck totals.
Unknown pricing is BYOK-only unless operator supplies a conservative override; platform eligibility fails closed.
Property tests prove totals are monotonic as price, token cap, discussion cycles, or AI seat count increase.
userStories.notes: Foundation for $5 admission and UI estimate.

userStories.title: OpenRouter adapter contract and opt-in real integration coverage
userStories.description: Close the provider foundation with recorded/stubbed contract tests and opt-in live tests that prove representative structured and non-structured models can take real Padrino turns.
acceptanceCriteria: Default tests cover success, invalid JSON coercion, structured response_format, provider fallback metadata, 402/403 budget errors, 429 retry, timeout, empty content, and cost extraction without network.
Opt-in integration tests use OPENROUTER_API_KEY, a hard per-run cost ceiling, and are marked integration/live_llm so Ralph/CI never spends real credit.
At least one structured and one non-structured affordable model exercise vote and night-action observations.
No integration cassette or failure output contains the API key or Authorization header.
A compatibility report can be generated from results without changing ranked eligibility automatically.
userStories.notes: Wave 15 provider contract gate.

userStories.title: Pure funding, credential, and promotional-credit policy
userStories.description: Define fail-closed typed decisions for PLATFORM_PROMO versus BYOK_OWNER, verified-account eligibility, one-time grant, model eligibility, reservation, and bounded completion reserve.
acceptanceCriteria: Pure facts/decision types choose exactly one funding source and stable denial reason; missing/unknown facts deny.
Promotional grant amount is exactly 5_000_000 USD micros and requires a verified non-deleted account; guests never receive it.
BYOK requires an active credential owned by the lobby host and never checks/consumes promo balance.
Platform admission requires compatible/allowed models and reservation <= available promo; completion reserve is operator money and cannot make player balance negative.
Custom host is payer for every AI seat; ranked/scientific funding modes remain server-owned and are not selectable here.
userStories.notes: Core policy only; persistence follows.

userStories.title: Encrypted provider credential schema (migration 0069)
userStories.description: Migration 0069 adds principal-owned provider credential and PKCE-flow tables designed for envelope encryption and rotation without storing plaintext.
acceptanceCriteria: 0069 follows 0068 linearly with SQLite/Postgres round-trip tests.

Credential row stores principal/provider, ciphertext, nonce, key_version, non-secret display suffix/label, created/updated/last_validated/revoked timestamps, and uniqueness for one active OpenRouter connection per principal.
PKCE flow stores only hashed/signed verifier binding, state/expiry/consumed status and is single-use under races.
No plaintext key column, ORM repr, index, audit row, or migration default exists.
Cascade/GDPR behavior revokes/deletes ciphertext without touching game events/replay.
userStories.notes: Use existing cryptography dependency; no KMS SDK required.

userStories.title: Envelope encryption, rotation, and secret-redaction service
userStories.description: Implement AES-GCM/Fernet-equivalent authenticated envelope encryption using a dedicated deployment master-key ring, with versioned decrypt and online rotation in the impure credentials layer.
acceptanceCriteria: Settings require a dedicated high-entropy credential master key for OpenRouter connect; missing/invalid key makes connect/BYOK unavailable but does not stop casual mock/platform boot.
Encrypt/decrypt authenticates principal id, provider, and credential id as associated context so ciphertext swapping fails.
Rotation decrypts with old active versions and rewrites with current version transactionally; raw values have shortest practical lifetime.
Exceptions/logging/repr/API serialization are redacted; tests use sentinel secrets and assert absence across captured logs, tracebacks, DB stringification, exports, events, and JSON responses.
Core imports no cryptography/settings and no new runtime dependency is added.
userStories.notes: Treat server memory as trusted impure boundary; never cache plaintext across games.

userStories.title: OpenRouter OAuth PKCE connect, status, and disconnect
userStories.description: Add a separate OpenRouter connection flow (not identity OAuth) that exchanges an authorization code server-side, encrypts the returned user-controlled key, validates it, and exposes only connection status.
acceptanceCriteria: Start endpoint creates S256 PKCE with signed session/principal-bound state and exact callback allowlist; callback is single-use/replay-resistant.
Callback exchanges code through MockTransport-tested HTTPS client, encrypts key before commit, and never returns key to browser/logs.
GET status returns connected, label/suffix, validated_at, and optional safe credit capability; POST disconnect revokes local credential and best-effort upstream key when supported.
CSRF, wrong principal/session, expired flow, callback replay, provider error, and DB failure all fail closed without orphan plaintext.
Terms/privacy and consent registry are updated if credential storage changes disclosed processing.
userStories.notes: Do not reuse general account OAuth access tokens.

userStories.title: Per-principal BYOK routing and isolation
userStories.description: Resolve the custom lobby host's encrypted OpenRouter credential only while constructing its AI adapters, and stamp every resulting call BYOK_OWNER.
acceptanceCriteria: A BYOK lobby decrypts only its host-owned active credential and uses it for all AI seats; invitees' credentials are never queried.
Adapter/runtime objects carry secret value only in impure memory and persistence stores credential id/funding source, never raw key.
Two concurrent games owned by different principals cannot cross-use credentials; sentinel-key tests inspect outgoing Authorization headers and DB/log/event outputs.
Revocation before launch denies launch; revocation after an admitted game follows the explicit provider-failure/no-contest path without falling back to platform key.
Every BYOK LlmCall is stamped funding_source=BYOK_OWNER and excluded from promotional ledger charges.
userStories.notes: Credential owner reference is frozen in lobby runtime snapshot.

userStories.title: Promotional credit ledger and reservations (migration 0070)
userStories.description: Migration 0070 introduces append-only integer-micro grant/charge/release/adjustment ledger rows plus game-scoped reservation state and an operator completion-reserve ledger.
acceptanceCriteria: 0070 follows 0069 linearly on SQLite/Postgres and adds constraints preventing negative amounts where invalid, duplicate idempotency keys, multiple promo grants per principal, and multiple active reservations per game.
Balance is derived from append-only entries; no mutable float balance column is authoritative.
Reservation stores estimate/catalog/rules hashes, reserved/consumed/released micros, status, principal, lobby/game ids, and timestamps outside core.
Completion reserve entries are separated from player ledger and attributable to estimate miss/game/model without exposing player PII publicly.
Repository tests prove ledger conservation and idempotent retry semantics.
userStories.notes: Use Numeric only for legacy cost rows; new monetary authority is integer micros.

userStories.title: Atomic one-time $5 grant and wallet API
userStories.description: Grant promotional credit lazily/idempotently to verified accounts and expose a safe wallet summary used by admission and UI.
acceptanceCriteria: First eligible request creates exactly one 5_000_000-micro grant; concurrent requests create one grant on Postgres/SQLite.
Guests, unverified/deleted/banned-from-credit accounts receive no grant with stable reason; ranked ban and credit-abuse ban remain distinct facts if needed.
Wallet response returns granted, available, reserved, spent, completion subsidy, and ledger-safe recent entries; it never includes raw credential/subkey/provider secrets.
GDPR delete tombstones public identity but preserves legally/accounting-required non-PII monetary audit according to documented code policy.
Rate limits prevent grant/wallet probing abuse.
userStories.notes: Formal promotions/legal review is required before public marketing but not code implementation.

userStories.title: Optional per-account OpenRouter limited subkeys
userStories.description: Add an optional management-key integration that provisions a platform inference subkey limited to the account's promotional allowance, while keeping Padrino's ledger authoritative and supporting deployments without a management key.
acceptanceCriteria: Management key is configured separately and cannot be used for completions; inference key cannot call management operations in tests/contracts.
Provisioning creates one idempotent account-scoped key with USD limit/expiry/allowlist where API supports it, encrypts returned plaintext once, and stores only management hash/metadata afterward.
If management integration is absent/unavailable, platform calls use the server inference key behind Padrino reservation controls; behavior is explicit in health/admin status.
Revocation/delete/credit exhaustion disables or deletes the subkey best-effort without blocking local settlement.
MockTransport tests cover create-once, timeout-after-create reconciliation, rotation, upstream 403/429, and no-secret outputs.
userStories.notes: Defense in depth, not the sole balance authority.

userStories.title: Atomic funding preflight and game reservation
userStories.description: Before locking/launching a funded custom game, resolve funding facts, compatibility, catalog/rules snapshots, estimate, wallet, credential, and atomically reserve the whole-game amount.
acceptanceCriteria: Platform promo launch succeeds only when reservation estimate fits available micros and every chosen model is platform-eligible; expensive/unpriced models return BYOK-required reasons.
BYOK launch requires explicit user-confirmed maximum estimate but creates no promo reservation.
Concurrent lobby launches cannot overspend one principal; exactly one wins when balance fits one game.
A failed launch releases reservation; an idempotent launch reuses the same reservation/game and cannot double reserve.
Funding/model/rules/catalog snapshot hashes are bound together so changing selection invalidates a stale quote/confirmation.
userStories.notes: Reservation must happen before Game/event creation.

userStories.title: Bounded operator completion reserve without model swaps
userStories.description: Guarantee that an admitted platform-funded game continues with its frozen models when actual cost exceeds its player reservation, bounded by a configurable per-game and global operator completion reserve.
acceptanceCriteria: Player ledger consumption stops at reserved/available promotional amount and never becomes negative.
Estimate miss creates explicit operator completion-reserve charges up to both per-game and global hard caps; no selected model or routing policy is changed.

If the operator reserve itself is exhausted, the runner records deterministic provider_unfunded/coerced actions and completes or no-contests according to persisted policy without charging the player further.
New games are denied while global completion reserve/breaker is open; already admitted games are not evicted.
Tests cover exact boundary, concurrent overruns, restart/reconciliation, and invariants under repeated settlement.
userStories.notes: Recommended policy locked by user.

userStories.title: Idempotent call charging and terminal settlement
userStories.description: Bind each persisted LlmCall to exactly one funding settlement, consume reservations as calls commit, reconcile OpenRouter-reported cost, and release unused reservation at terminal/no-contest.
acceptanceCriteria: Each billable call has a unique charge idempotency key and integer-micro amount derived from provider response cost or versioned conservative table.
PLATFORM charges consume player reservation then operator completion reserve; BYOK charges are audited but never debit promo.
Terminal settlement releases unused micros once and marks reservation terminal in the same durable workflow as game completion or via self-healing reconciliation.
Crash windows before/after LlmCall commit, charge commit, and game terminal status converge without duplicate/missing charges.
Existing funding_source field is populated accurately for all human-lane calls and cost reports sum byte-stably.
userStories.notes: Financial correctness blocker.

userStories.title: Credential/credit GDPR, retention, and operational audit
userStories.description: Extend export/delete/retention/admin health without exposing secrets or losing required accounting, and add a reusable secret scanner regression over all player-visible/archive surfaces.
acceptanceCriteria: Human export reports connection metadata and wallet ledger facts but never ciphertext, nonce, key material, management hashes usable as credentials, or raw authorization errors.
Delete revokes credentials/subkeys, erases ciphertext and PKCE flows, releases cancellable reservations, and preserves pseudonymized required charge audit/replay.
Retention removes expired flows/revoked ciphertext on configured TTL; dry-run/executor counts are idempotent.
Health/admin status reports catalog freshness, encryption readiness, management integration, promo liability, reservations, and completion reserve without PII/secrets.
A sentinel secret test scans logs, events, replay/export JSON, API reads, analytics, and frontend fixtures for absence.
userStories.notes: Coordinate legal document content hashes so users re-consent when required.

userStories.title: Neo-noir occult laboratory design system
userStories.description: Create the cohesive consumer visual foundation: deep ink/obsidian surfaces, candle/ember accents, restrained cyan/violet instrumentation, typographic hierarchy, role/faction tokens, atmospheric but accessible effects, and reusable game components.
acceptanceCriteria: Design tokens/components cover color, typography, spacing, elevation, focus, status, role/faction, model badges, cards, dialogs, tooltips, tabs, skeletons, toasts, and data displays in light-independent dark-first theme.
No hidden role/human/model information is encoded by color, motion, sound, DOM attributes, asset URLs, or accessibility labels before reveal.
All text/control contrast meets WCAG AA; focus-visible and keyboard behavior are tested; reduced-motion and high-contrast modes are first-class.
Assets are repo-native SVG/CSS/static files with licensing/source notes in code where needed; no runtime image generation.
Visual regression screenshots pin desktop/mobile core components and eliminate raw UUID/admin-form styling.
userStories.notes: Frontend story: run lint/check/e2e.

userStories.title: Game-mode home and first-run onboarding
userStories.description: Redesign home around Quick Play, Custom Lobby, and Ranked (ranked preview remains disabled until Wave 16), with concise rules/onboarding and funding state.
acceptanceCriteria: Three mode cards clearly explain audience, rating status, configuration freedom, expected duration, and funding; Custom never implies ranked.
First-run onboarding teaches day/chat/vote/night/reveal in under two minutes and can be reopened/skipped.
Quick Play lets the user choose platform promo or connected OpenRouter then obtains a bound quote before match creation.
Empty/loading/error/offline states are branded and actionable rather than dashboard dashes/raw API errors.
Desktop/mobile Playwright covers guest consent, verified wallet, connected BYOK, exhausted credit, and ranked-coming-next states.
userStories.notes: Do not enable Wave16 ranked routes.

userStories.title: Visual OpenRouter model explorer and comparison
userStories.description: Build a fast searchable selector that makes hundreds of OpenRouter models understandable and exciting while exposing price/reliability/privacy honestly.
acceptanceCriteria: Virtualized/searchable cards show name/provider, description, context, price per million, estimated game range, latency/throughput when available, privacy/ZDR, availability, and tier/reason badges.
Filters cover provider, free/price band, structured compatibility, context, speed, open-weight/frontier, platform-eligible, BYOK-only, and ranked-qualified preview.
Users can compare at least three models and select by canonical slug; no internal AgentBuild/ModelConfig UUID appears.
Unverified models require a clear casual reliability confirmation; extreme/unpriced models require BYOK and spend confirmation.
Keyboard/screen-reader/mobile interactions and stale-catalog/error states have Playwright coverage.
userStories.notes: Frontend/API integration story.

userStories.title: Visual custom table and role-deck builder
userStories.description: Replace the plain custom lobby form with a staged table builder for rules, roles, humans, AI models, cadence, identity, theme, and funding.
acceptanceCriteria: Host chooses built-in preset or edits supported role cards with live validation/explanation; UI never assigns a chosen person a role.
Table displays configurable human invitation slots and AI model slots; model cards drag/select into AI slots and duplicates are allowed.
Quote updates when deck/cadence/model mix changes and launch confirmation binds quote hash plus maximum spend/funding source.
Anonymous/transparent explanation distinguishes pregame roster knowledge from hidden in-game seat mapping.
Invalid decks, full human capacity, unavailable models, stale quotes, disconnected BYOK, and insufficient promo are resolved inline with no raw server tokens.
userStories.notes: Primary custom-game setup UX.

userStories.title: Truthful waiting room, invitations, ready-up, and host controls
userStories.description: Redesign the lobby room around actual seated humans and configured AI slots, with display names, invitations, presence, ready state, safe model/deck summary, kick/leave/host transfer, and launch readiness.
acceptanceCriteria: Every member row corresponds to one HUMAN LobbySeat and shows display label/self/host/presence/ready; UI never shows UUID as the primary identity.
AI roster shows selected model cards before launch without binding them to future public seat ids.
Invite copy/share, join, leave, kick, host transfer, reconnect, capacity, and stale eviction update through SSE without polling-only races.
Launch button uses server readiness reasons and cannot start if any member is unseated/not ready or funding/model quote stale.
Ranked controls are absent; custom room is clearly casual.
userStories.notes: Frontend story with multi-browser Playwright contexts.

userStories.title: Atmospheric responsive play table
userStories.description: Replace the three-column dashboard with a social table optimized for conversation: character portraits, readable pseudonyms, self role card, alive/graveyard state, chat, vote/action affordances, phase clock, connection, and optional technical inspector.
acceptanceCriteria: Desktop table spatially presents all seats and mobile uses purpose-built table/chat/action views without losing state.
Self role/faction/legal actions are prominent and accessible; other hidden roles/human-model identity remain absent pre-reveal.
Elimination, reconnect/takeover notice, terminal, errors, and no-action phases are clear and do not strand navigation.
A secondary inspector exposes game/rules/model-count/replay-safe metadata without dominating play or leaking identity.
Existing action/chat/idempotency/SSE behavior remains functional and Playwright covers representative day/night roles.
userStories.notes: Do not rewrite mechanics in frontend.

userStories.title: Conversation, vote, phase motion, and optional sound
userStories.description: Add the game-feel layer for paced 20–30 minute play: chat bubbles, speaker focus, phase transitions, vote movement/tally, night ambience, countdown urgency, and sound controls.
acceptanceCriteria: Released chat animates in committed sequence order; animation timing never reveals whether author is human/AI or provider latency.
Vote review/confirm/tally/elimination motion matches committed frames and survives reconnect without replaying misleading effects.
Day/night/terminal transitions and countdown use phase snapshot/deadline only; no client-derived mechanical state.
Sound is off or conservative by default, user-muted persistently, has captions/visual equivalents, and respects reduced-motion/data preferences.
Deterministic UI tests use synthetic frames and Playwright asserts no duplicate/lost chat/vote across reconnect.
userStories.notes: Frontend-only presentation over existing committed events.

userStories.title: Reveal ceremony, model cards, and funding receipt
userStories.description: Turn terminal reveal into the payoff: role/faction story, human-vs-AI guesses, exact model identities, routed-provider facts, performance/cost receipt, replay link, and rematch/custom-copy actions.
acceptanceCriteria: Reveal is inaccessible pre-terminal and then shows every seat's role, human/AI provenance, selected model plus actual routed provider/model where allowed, and takeover history.
Costs are grouped by model/seat/funding source with player promo debit, BYOK audited spend, completion subsidy, reservation release, and totals; no credential metadata appears.
Spot-the-AI result and personal stats update once; rematch copies casual configuration into a new unlocked lobby with fresh seed/quote.
Scientific details are expandable and clearly distinguish requested model from provider routing.
Mobile/desktop, reduced-motion, privacy full-JSON, and replay-link tests pass.
userStories.notes: Exact provider identity opens only at endgame.

userStories.title: Mobile, accessibility, performance, and visual regression gate
userStories.description: Run a cross-product hardening pass over the complete casual product rather than treating responsiveness/accessibility as per-page cleanup.
acceptanceCriteria: Playwright covers 390x844 and desktop for home, model explorer, builder, waiting room, live day/night, elimination, reveal, wallet, and connection flows.
Automated accessibility plus manual-testable landmarks/names/focus order/live regions show no serious violations; all mechanics work keyboard-only.
Catalog virtualization and live table stay within defined DOM/render budgets; no unbounded SSE/chat/catalog growth.
Screenshots pin the locked neo-noir technical direction for core states and reduced-motion mode.
CORS/base URL/session cookie production configuration has a smoke test so local/deployed UI does not show Failed to fetch under documented setup.
userStories.notes: Frontend gates mandatory.

userStories.title: Wave 15 full casual-product release gate
userStories.description: One adversarial gate proves the complete Wave 15 promise before any Wave 16 story may start. It is a verification/test story, not a feature catch-all.
acceptanceCriteria: A cold verified user can receive promo, configure a supported custom role deck and named OpenRouter models, invite at least one other human, ready, launch, play with stubbed provider transport to terminal, reveal, settle, and replay.
A connected-BYOK variant completes with a different principal and proves credential isolation/no promo debit; a platform variant proves reservation and bounded estimate-miss subsidy.
Quick Play completes on desktop/mobile; custom multi-human composition is truthful; custom games write zero HumanRating/HumanRatingEvent/Rating/RatingEvent.
Rules/runtime/catalog/routing/funding snapshots plus event chain verify deterministically after rehydration; sentinel credentials are absent from every persisted/user-visible surface.
All backend and frontend gates pass; opt-in real OpenRouter smoke is documented as operator preflight but not required by default CI.
userStories.notes: Every Wave 16 story depends directly or transitively on US-373.

userStories.title: Enforce the final game-mode taxonomy
userStories.description: Make Casual Quick Play, Casual Custom, Ranked Solo, Ranked Mixed, and Scientific AI explicit server-owned modes rather than overloading Lobby.ranked/stakes booleans. Remove the ranked checkbox and ranked launch path from custom lobbies.
acceptanceCriteria: A pure GameMode policy defines allowed league kind, rating scope, invite/party behavior, player configuration, identity mode, and funding authority for every mode.
Custom/quickplay routes always create casual non-rating games and reject ranked fields/legacy attempts; no hidden request can mint ranked custom games.
Existing ranked human rows remain readable/migratable, but all new ranked games must enter dedicated Wave 16 endpoints.
Scientific AI mode remains gauntlet/campaign-only and cannot contain human seats.
API/frontend tests show distinct mode labels and prove custom opponent/role selection cannot reach any ranked writer.
userStories.notes: Wave 16 root story; closes the old custom ranked exploit.

userStories.title: Pure ranked season, pool, and scope contracts
userStories.description: Define immutable pure contracts for ranked season identity, SOLO_HUMAN_VS_AI and MIXED_HUMAN_AI scopes, server rules/cadence snapshot, frozen model pool, AI anchors, role/faction calibration, eligibility, and lifecycle.
acceptanceCriteria: Season config is frozen/hash-addressed and includes mode, ruleset/rules hash, cadence hash, pool hash, calibration hash, starts/ends, placement threshold, and policy version.
Season states DRAFT, SHADOW, ACTIVE, FROZEN, CLOSED have deterministic allowed transitions with injected time/facts.
Solo and mixed scopes are distinct keys; ratings/events from one cannot satisfy or affect another.
Season pool entries include immutable AgentRuntimeSnapshot identity, fixed AI anchor mu/sigma, weight/schedule quota, provider policy, and qualification evidence hash.
Pure validation rejects custom rules, player-selected routing, missing anchors/calibration, overlapping active scope, and non-ranked-qualified pool entries.
userStories.notes: Core only; persistence next.

userStories.title: Ranked season and pool persistence (migration 0071)
userStories.description: Migration 0071 adds ranked seasons, immutable pool entries, role/faction calibration, and lifecycle audit rows. It establishes one active season per mode/ruleset without altering scientific ratings.
acceptanceCriteria: 0071 follows 0070 linearly with SQLite/Postgres upgrade/downgrade and migration-head tests.
Tables persist every season snapshot/hash field and append-only transition audit; pool/calibration rows are immutable after SHADOW.
Partial unique constraints prevent overlapping ACTIVE seasons for the same mode/ruleset while allowing drafts/history.
No raw provider credential, player identity, or scientific Rating foreign key is stored; AI anchors are copied values with provenance snapshot ids.
Repository create/transition/read paths are transactional, idempotent, and fail closed on hash disagreement.
userStories.notes: Ranked season is impure configuration; core consumes frozen facts.

userStories.title: Ranked model qualification from evidence and drift
userStories.description: Turn the Wave 15 preview tier into an enforceable, versioned ranked qualification process bound to catalog, probe, prompt/schema, provider endpoint, price, latency, privacy, and drift evidence.
acceptanceCriteria: Admin qualification evaluates the pure tier policy and writes append-only qualified/refused evidence with operator/policy version and reason tokens.
Qualification pins an exact canonical slug and provider endpoint/routing policy with allow_fallbacks=false, require_parameters=true, ZDR/data policy, max price, and inference params.
Catalog/provider/prompt/schema/price/latency drift marks future season eligibility stale without mutating an existing frozen season.
At least N successful contract probes across required role/action families is enforced from settings/policy.
Human and scientific ranked launch both refuse an unqualified or stale model unless already frozen into an active season under its grandfather policy.
userStories.notes: Automated decisions are qualification only, not anti-cheat penalties.

userStories.title: Exact-route OpenRouter scientific agent builds and campaigns
userStories.description: Enable AI-only scientific gauntlets/campaigns to recruit ranked-qualified OpenRouter models while preserving exact attribution and the existing canonical rating firewall.
acceptanceCriteria: Scientific materialization freezes catalog/qualification/prompt/schema/provider endpoint/inference/routing hashes into AgentBuild/campaign cells.
Requests disable router/provider/model fallback unless an explicit experiment config defines a labeled fallback arm; require_parameters and router metadata are on.
Actual provider/model/attempt metadata and cost persist per call; an unexpected actual model/provider makes the game non-publishable rather than crediting the requested build.
Existing paired/mirrored scheduling and model/ruleset-specific Rating writes remain unchanged and human tables are untouched.
Deterministic stubbed heterogeneous campaign plus opt-in live mini-gauntlet cover the new path.
userStories.notes: AI-only ranked already exists; this story opens the OpenRouter field safely.

userStories.title: Freeze calibrated ranked AI pools from scientific evidence
userStories.description: Build an admin service that selects qualified models and copies scientific evidence into an immutable season pool/AI-anchor snapshot without creating a runtime dependency from human games to scientific tables.
acceptanceCriteria: Pool builder runs outside human game hot paths, reads publishable scientific ratings/evidence, and copies anchor mu/sigma/provenance into season pool rows.
Selection enforces provider/model diversity, role/faction coverage, qualification freshness, cost/latency/privacy ceilings, and configurable schedule weights.
Same inputs/policy produce identical pool ordering/hash; manual inclusions/exclusions are explicit audit facts.
After freeze, changing scientific Rating rows cannot change an existing season pool or any human rating delta.
Tests install SQL listeners around human runtime/writer paths proving they never query Rating/RatingEvent.
userStories.notes: Bridge by snapshot copy only; hard rule 14.

userStories.title: Admin season lifecycle, shadow activation, and kill switches
userStories.description: Provide admin-only create/inspect/validate/transition endpoints and independent default-off kill switches for ranked solo and ranked mixed.
acceptanceCriteria: Settings have separate solo/mixed enabled flags default False plus global human-rating kill switch; all must permit admission/write.
Admin can create DRAFT, validate hashes/pool/calibration, enter SHADOW, activate, freeze, and close with transition audit; invalid transitions fail.
Only one ACTIVE season per mode/ruleset is returned to matchmaking; SHADOW produces no public rating writes.
Turning any relevant flag off blocks new admission and rechecks at rating write for in-flight games without deploy.
Responses use model/season facts but no secret refs/raw credentials; auth/pagination/audit tests pass.
userStories.notes: Production remains OFF after Wave 16 implementation.

userStories.title: Ranked solo admission and match endpoint
userStories.description: Add a dedicated verified-account ranked solo endpoint that composes existing fail-closed identity/consent/ban checks with active season, queue/admission, and server-owned config.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /human/ranked/solo/match requires account, verified email, current base+ranked consent, no active ban, flags enabled, and active SOLO season; denial reason ordering is pinned.
Guests are directed to sign-in/consent without minting ranked state; request accepts no model, role, rules, routing, identity, cadence, or funding override.
The game is anonymous, strangers-only one-human plus AI, season/rules/pool scoped, and funded by server-ranked budget—not promo/BYOK.
Admission and materialization are idempotent; concurrent requests cannot create multiple active ranked matches for one principal.
Custom/private lobby tables and invite tokens are not used as ranked authority.
userStories.notes: Can internally reuse launch primitives with a dedicated ranked match owner/config.

userStories.title: Deterministic balanced solo schedule and role assignment
userStories.description: Assign each ranked solo entrant a role/faction and AI roster through a deterministic, auditable schedule that balances exposure across placement/ranked games without letting the client reroll.
acceptanceCriteria: Pure scheduler derives role/faction quota cell and AI pool draw from season id, principal pseudonymous schedule key, completed-count ledger, and server seed; same inputs match.
Repeated cancellations/no-shows do not freely reroll favorable roles/models; consumed/reserved schedule cells have explicit lifecycle.
Over a configured cycle, exposure matches season role/faction and model-weight quotas within pinned tolerance.
AI seat duplicates follow pool policy; public pre-reveal surfaces expose neither selected models nor schedule cell.
A schedule ledger/audit persists enough facts for replay/rating recompute without raw email/device identity.
userStories.notes: Fairness and anti-cherry-pick blocker.

userStories.title: Pure season-scoped solo rating with role/faction calibration
userStories.description: Define the ranked solo update using human prior, frozen AI anchors, actual faction result, scheduled role/faction baseline, placement/forfeit facts, and policy version. It must be deterministic and independent of live scientific rows.
acceptanceCriteria: Pure function consumes only frozen season facts plus prior and outcome, returning new rating/event inputs; no DB/settings/clock/random.
Expected result is adjusted by pinned role/faction calibration and AI table anchors so harder assignments yield fairer updates; math/ranges are documented in code and golden-tested.
Win/loss/draw, day-cap, no-contest, disconnect takeover forfeit, and invalid/insufficient participation have explicit outcomes; forfeit overrides faction win/draw.
Calibration cannot produce non-finite/negative sigma or unbounded delta; property tests cover symmetry/monotonicity/bounds.
Identical event stream recomputes byte-identically and different live scientific ratings have no effect.
userStories.notes: Use OpenSkill primitives where appropriate, but freeze policy/constants.

userStories.title: Season/mode-scoped human rating storage (migration 0072)
userStories.description: Migration 0072 scopes HumanRating/HumanRatingEvent by season, mode, and ruleset and archives complete rating inputs needed for solo/mixed recomputation while preserving legacy Wave 14 rows.
acceptanceCriteria: 0072 follows 0071 linearly, upgrades/downgrades SQLite/Postgres, and assigns legacy rows to an explicit LEGACY_SOLO scope without fabricating an active season.

Uniqueness includes principal/human player, season, mode, ruleset; events include prior/posterior, outcome, role/faction, AI anchor/pool/calibration/policy hashes, participation/forfeit/no-contest, and idempotency.
Existing public ladder can still read legacy rows but new ranked routes always filter explicit scope.
No FK/read dependency to scientific Rating/RatingEvent is introduced.
ORM/repository/migration tests cover isolation across two seasons and two modes.
userStories.notes: May rename sibling tables only through additive migration/backfill, never edit old migrations.

userStories.title: Idempotent ranked solo finalize and provenance
userStories.description: Wire terminal solo games to the new writer with write-time season/flag/consent/ban/config rechecks, schedule settlement, rating event, and applied/refused provenance.
acceptanceCriteria: Exactly one rating event per game/principal/scope commits with terminal game persistence or converges through idempotent reconciliation.
Writer rechecks global+solo flags, active/grandfather season, consent withdrawal, ban, game config hashes, schedule cell, and replay-valid terminal outcome; refusal writes provenance and no rating.
AI takeover writes a forfeit loss; technical/provider-budget no-contest writes no rating and returns schedule cell according to policy.
Eligible write touches only season-scoped human tables/audits and performs zero scientific table reads/writes under SQL listener test.
Rollback/retry/crash tests prove no duplicate delta or lost terminal game.
userStories.notes: Extends Wave14 defenses rather than bypassing them.

userStories.title: Ranked solo queue and post-match UI
userStories.description: Enable the Ranked mode card for eligible users and build a focused solo flow: eligibility, season/pool disclosure, consent, search/preparation, live game, and rating result.
acceptanceCriteria: UI explains standardized server-selected opponents/roles, active season/ruleset, anonymity, provisional threshold, disconnect forfeit, and no player funding.
Eligibility failures route to sign-in, verified email, ranked consent, ban/support, disabled/season-unavailable states with human copy.
No model/role/routing controls appear; network retry is idempotent and cancel cannot reroll consumed schedule unfairly.
Post-match shows prior/delta/new score, provisional progress, role/faction baseline context, season rank, and no-contest/refusal reason when applicable.
Mobile/desktop/reduced-motion Playwright covers placement win/loss, forfeit, flag-off, consent withdrawal, and reconnect.
userStories.notes: Frontend gates mandatory.

userStories.title: Ranked solo deterministic end-to-end and shadow proof
userStories.description: Prove the entire ranked solo product in default tests and shadow mode before mixed queue work.
acceptanceCriteria: Cold verified account completes ranked consent, enters an active synthetic season, receives balanced server config, plays to terminal, and gets exactly one scoped rating.
Second game exercises another role/faction schedule cell; schedule/rating/replay remain stable across rehydration.
Player cannot alter model/role/rules/cadence/funding via request tampering and pre-reveal identity stays blind.
Flag-off/ban/withdrawal after game creation blocks write with provenance; AI takeover becomes forfeit; provider failure becomes no-contest.
SHADOW season runs identical decision math/audit but writes no public HumanRating and does not appear on leaderboard.
userStories.notes: Solo release candidate gate.

userStories.title: Pure mixed-ranked queue and table policy
userStories.description: Define the strangers-only mixed human/AI queue policy: solo entrants, minimum/target humans, wait/backfill thresholds, ruleset/region/language compatibility, blocks, rematch avoidance, and server ownership.
acceptanceCriteria: Policy accepts only eligible solo principals with matching active MIXED season/config and returns deterministic compatible grouping decisions from injected tickets/time.
No invite, party, friend, host, model, role, team, provider, cadence, funding, or seat preference is accepted.

Initial policy defaults are 4 humans / target 7 / 90-second AI-backfill threshold for mini7 and 6 humans / target 10 / 120 seconds for bench10; values are season-configured and shadow-calibrated, and a match never starts below minimum.
Recent co-player avoidance and mutual blocks are hard constraints; soft latency/language/skill bands widen deterministically with wait.
Policy returns stable reason/explanation tokens and imports no DB/clock/random.
userStories.notes: Initial parties explicitly out of scope.

userStories.title: Persistent ranked queue tickets and claims (migration 0073)
userStories.description: Migration 0073 adds durable mixed-ranked tickets, leases/claims, readiness checks, and match membership so API/worker restarts cannot duplicate or strand entrants.
acceptanceCriteria: 0073 follows 0072 linearly with SQLite/Postgres round-trip and indexes for active season/status/created/lease.
One active ticket per principal/mode/season is enforced; ticket stores non-PII matching facts, policy hash, state timestamps, lease owner/expiry, and cancellation/no-show provenance.
Match membership transactionally consumes tickets once and links the eventual game; stale leases are reaped without losing queue age.
No raw IP/email/device/display name or provider credential is stored; anti-cheat references use existing hashed/sidecar facts.
Repository concurrency tests prove disjoint workers cannot claim the same ticket/table.
userStories.notes: DB-as-queue, no Redis.

userStories.title: Mixed queue API, presence, ready check, and cancellation
userStories.description: Expose enter/status/stream/leave/ready endpoints with fail-closed eligibility and durable reconnect behavior suitable for multi-minute waits.
acceptanceCriteria: Enter reuses ranked identity/consent/ban/flag checks and is idempotent; status/SSE is principal-scoped and reveals only safe aggregate wait/table facts.
Presence heartbeat and disconnect grace prevent ghost matches; ready check has bounded timeout and explicit accept/decline/no-show states.
Cancellation before claim is immediate; after match reservation follows dodge policy and cannot be used to inspect/reroll roles/models.
A principal cannot queue in solo and mixed or multiple rulesets simultaneously under configured policy.
Rate limits and concurrency tests cover spam, duplicate tabs, restart, stale tickets, and cancel/claim races.
userStories.notes: No lobby host exists in mixed ranked.

userStories.title: Concurrent mixed table assembler and AI backfill
userStories.description: Implement the dedicated matchmaker worker step that claims compatible tickets, performs ready check, fills remaining seats from frozen pool after policy threshold, and atomically materializes one ranked human-lane game.
acceptanceCriteria: Assembler uses DB row claims/leases to build each table once across workers; failed readiness returns eligible tickets without resetting fair queue age and penalizes decliners per policy.
Human membership count meets policy; remaining AI selections follow season weights/quotas and frozen exact routing; no player can influence them.
Materialized Game/GameSeats carry season/mode/rules/pool/calibration/schedule/match hashes and no invite/lobby host authority.
Role/public-seat assignment is seeded after final membership and remains identity-blind; queue ordering cannot reveal faction/role.
Partial failure before game commit releases claims; after commit reconciliation links all memberships/tickets idempotently.
userStories.notes: Separate worker hook may share human lane process but not benchmark capacity.

userStories.title: Deterministic mixed seating with faction-exposure balancing
userStories.description: Balance human role/faction exposure over a season without assigning roles by rating, identity, model knowledge, or client choice. The final assignment remains seeded and auditable.
acceptanceCriteria: Pure assignment selects among valid seeded permutations using only season schedule deficits and a deterministic tie-break; it never reads ratings/display identity/chat.
Over quota cycles each human's role/faction exposure remains within configured tolerance without guaranteeing a requested role.
Assignment does not condition on intended winner, model strength, party, or live provider state and preserves the role deck exactly.
Schedule reservation prevents disconnect/cancel rerolls; no-show settlement is explicit.
Property/golden tests cover varying human counts, solo factions, impossible-balance fallback, and replay stability.
userStories.notes: Fairness scheduling is distinct from matchmaking skill bands.

userStories.title: Pure mixed human/AI team rating with frozen anchors
userStories.description: Implement season-scoped mixed rating over actual faction teams: human priors update, AI seats contribute frozen read-only anchor ratings, role/faction calibration adjusts expectations, and only humans persist.
acceptanceCriteria: Pure function accepts ordered teams with humans/AI anchors, ranks/outcome, roles, participation/forfeit, calibration and policy hashes; no DB/settings/clock/random.
OpenSkill team math handles multiple humans per faction and frozen AI anchors; AI posterior values are discarded and never written to scientific or human model rows.
Human deltas respond monotonically to result and expected team strength, remain bounded, and do not depend on live scientific ratings.
Draw, multi-faction/solo roles supported by season policy, all-human-one-faction tables, no-contest, multiple forfeits, and AI takeover are explicitly golden-tested.
Event output contains every prior/anchor/calibration input needed for byte-identical ordered recomputation.
userStories.notes: Use JOSS/OpenSkill multi-team principles but calibrate empirically in shadow.

userStories.title: Rating calibration simulator and golden corpus
userStories.description: Before persistence, build an offline deterministic simulator that stress-tests solo/mixed rating policy for bias, inflation, convergence, role imbalance, human-count mix, AI anchors, collusion patterns, and disconnects.
acceptanceCriteria: Seeded simulator generates controlled seasons from explicit synthetic skill/outcome models and returns calibration metrics without network/DB/real user data.
Tests assert no systematic rating gain for equal-skill population, bounded inflation/deflation, convergence ordering, role/faction residual within thresholds, and stable behavior across human counts.
Golden corpus covers current built-in ranked rulesets, solo and mixed, rare roles, draws/day caps, forfeits/no-contests, and season reset.
Policy/calibration changes intentionally update versioned goldens and cannot reinterpret old events.
A machine-readable report is available to shadow go/no-go and CI threshold checks.
userStories.notes: Scientific validity blocker, not a claim of perfect real-world calibration.

userStories.title: Idempotent multi-principal mixed rating finalize
userStories.description: Persist mixed updates for every eligible human in one terminal workflow with per-principal write-time rechecks and all-or-explicit-partial provenance, while retaining enough facts for global recompute.
acceptanceCriteria: One game produces at most one event per principal/scope and one immutable ordered game-rating input record; retry is idempotent.
Flags/season/config/replay are game-wide gates; consent/ban/withdrawal/forfeit eligibility is rechecked per principal and refusal does not silently erase other eligible audit facts.
Rating inputs use pregame priors frozen at match start/terminal policy as specified so concurrent games for one principal serialize deterministically.
No scientific tables are read/written; AI anchors come only from season snapshot.
Crash/concurrent finalize tests prove deterministic ordering, no duplicate deltas, and explicit reconciliation state.
userStories.notes: May serialize active ranked games per principal to avoid ambiguous concurrent priors.

userStories.title: No-show, dodge, disconnect, and multi-forfeit policy
userStories.description: Define and enforce player-facing consequences for ready-check decline/no-show, pregame dodge, midgame disconnect/takeover, reconnect, and infrastructure failure without confusing misconduct with provider faults.
acceptanceCriteria: Pure policy maps stage, presence, grace, prior strikes, and infrastructure facts to ticket cooldown, schedule settlement, rating forfeit/no-contest, and audit reasons.
A human taken over after grace receives forfeit loss even if faction wins/draws; connected teammates/opponents rate against the frozen replacement anchor as specified.
Provider/platform/worker failure affecting table fairness produces no-contest, no player strike, no rating, and restores appropriate schedule/queue facts.
Short reconnect within grace preserves control and cannot duplicate actions; repeated dodges escalate bounded cooldown but never auto-ban without review.
UI/API expose clear reason/duration/appeal path without revealing other players' identity or anti-cheat facts.
userStories.notes: Compose with existing takeover event/provenance.

userStories.title: Player reports, blocks, and mutes schema (migration 0074)
userStories.description: Add the minimum strangers-ranked safety substrate: post-game reports, principal blocks, and game-local mutes, segregated from hash-chained mechanics and public identity.
acceptanceCriteria: 0074 follows 0073 linearly and supports append-only reports with category/evidence refs/status, unique directional blocks, and game/principal mute sidecar state; upgrade/downgrade/index tests pass.
Reports reference pseudonymous principal/game/sidecar sequence without copying raw chat into hash-chain/audit payloads.
Block API cannot reveal whether another principal blocked the caller; matching uses mutual exclusion privately.
GDPR/retention distinguishes reporter safety evidence from ordinary chat and preserves deterministic event replay.
No report/block/mute action automatically changes ratings or imposes a ranked ban.
userStories.notes: Friends graph remains out of scope; blocking is safety-critical.

userStories.title: Report/block services and matchmaker enforcement
userStories.description: Expose authenticated report/block/unblock/mute flows, retain evidence safely, and enforce blocks in mixed matching without turning reports into automatic penalties.
acceptanceCriteria: Only game participants can report another participant for that completed/recent game; categories and bounded note/evidence references are validated/rate limited.
Block/unblock is idempotent; current/future matching never groups either direction while existing games remain replayable.
Mute hides sidecar chat locally and never suppresses structured actions/game events or leak mute state to target.
Admin review can inspect pseudonymous evidence under existing auth/audit; no public/raw display-name leak.
Abuse tests cover fabricated game/seat, report spam, block probing, deleted users, and retention.
userStories.notes: Manual moderation only.

userStories.title: Ranked chat safety and player controls UI
userStories.description: Add in-game mute and post-game report/block UX appropriate for anonymous ranked play, plus clear moderation/appeal expectations.
acceptanceCriteria: Mute is accessible from chat/seat context without revealing human/AI identity and has visible local state/undo.
Report becomes available only when target provenance is server-authorized; pre-reveal UI uses public seat id and server resolves principal privately.
Post-reveal block/report confirmations avoid raw UUID/email/display name and explain that reports do not automatically alter ratings.
Keyboard/mobile/screen-reader flows work and malicious text is escaped; sidecar moderation status remains private.
Playwright covers report, block preventing a future synthetic match, mute, rate-limit/error, and deleted-account cases.
userStories.notes: Frontend gates mandatory.

userStories.title: Mixed-ranked telemetry and advisory integrity signals
userStories.description: Extend advisory telemetry for a true multi-human environment: repeated co-play, coordinated voting/action timing, account/device/IP clusters, queue dodges, abnormal role-conditioned outcomes, and bot cadence—without automatic penalties.
acceptanceCriteria: Pure scorer uses injected window/thresholds and pseudonymous rows to emit deterministic flags/evidence; no rating/game mutation.
Signals distinguish teammates/opponents, expected queue rematches, NAT/shared-IP uncertainty, role/faction baselines, and infrastructure no-contests to reduce false positives.
Raw IP/chat/provider credentials never enter evidence; hashes and bounded aggregates only.
Batch/admin capture is savepoint-isolated and cannot block game/rating writes; failure emits metric/audit.
Threshold/below-threshold/property tests and multi-human synthetic collusion fixtures pass; flags remain manual-review only.
userStories.notes: Wave14 scorer evolves from one-human assumptions.

userStories.title: Season-stream rating exclusion and deterministic recompute (migration 0075)
